title: From v3.0.0 the Helm chart version equals the controller version (chart 1.17 → 3.0) — pinned chart ranges and tooling break
quote: Helm Chart Version Alignment: Helm chart version now aligns with LBC version. Previously, LBC v2.x used Helm chart v1.x (e.g., LBC v2.17 = Helm v1.17). Starting with v3.0.0, both versions match.**
remediation: Update every chart-version pin (HelmRelease / Argo CD Application targetRevision, Terraform helm_release version, renovate rules) from the 1.x line to 3.x; a constraint like ~1.17 never resolves the new release. The app version is unchanged in meaning.
verifyCommand: kubectl get secret -A -l owner=helm,name=aws-load-balancer-controller -o json | jq -r '.items[] | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) chart=\(.metadata.labels.version // "-") status=\(.metadata.labels.status)"'  # the installed chart version per Helm release

title: Chart 1.15–1.17 (LBC 2.15–2.17) with enableCertManager=true deleted the Certificate that renews aws-load-balancer-tls — the webhook certificate expires; v3.0.0 restores it

detection.reason: whether the chart runs with enableCertManager is not projected; the hint names the controller Deployment and the command checks the Certificate exists and is renewing

quote: Issue: #4359 attempted to fix a race condition in webhook certificate renewal but introduced a critical bug. The aws-load-balancer-tls Secret persists but the Certificate that owned and renewed it was removed, causing eventual certificate expiration and webhook TLS failures (#4541). This prevents the controller from updating target group bindings and can lead to outages. This bug impacts users deploying with Helm and utilizing the enableCertManager=true flag.
remediation: Upgrade to v3.0.0 or newer, which reinstates the Certificate (keepTLSSecret is removed from the chart). Users staying on the 1.15–1.17 charts (LBC 2.15–2.17) with cert-manager must set keepTLSSecret=false. After the upgrade confirm cert-manager owns aws-load-balancer-serving-cert again; an expired aws-load-balancer-tls Secret stops every LBC webhook, and with failurePolicy Fail pod and Service creation with it.
verifyCommand: kubectl get certificate -A -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("aws-load-balancer")) | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) ready=\((.status.conditions // [])[] | select(.type == "Ready") | .status) notAfter=\(.status.notAfter // "-")"'; kubectl get secret -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.metadata.name == "aws-load-balancer-tls") | "\(.metadata.namespace)/\(.metadata.name) owner=\((.metadata.ownerReferences // [])[0].kind // "none")"'  # with cert-manager the Secret must be owned by a Certificate; owner=none means nothing renews it
coversNotes: v3.0.0 (Webhook Certificate Issu): Action for users upgrading to v3.0.0: No action required - th
v3.0.0 (Enhancements and Fixes): Webhook Certificate: Reverted race condition fix in webhook cer

title: Gateway API support is GA in v3.0.0 and built against Gateway API v1.3.0 CRDs — install them before the controller

detection.reason: checked the Gateway API CRDs' bundle-version annotation — a bundle below v1.3.0 is older than what v3.0 is built against

remediation: Apply the Gateway API v1.3.0 standard CRDs (experimental-install for TCPRoute/UDPRoute/TLSRoute) and the LBC gateway CRDs (config/crd/gateway/gateway-crds.yaml) before upgrading the controller.

gate.reason: the Gateway API CRD requirement only bites clusters that run Gateway API routes under this controller — with no route of any kind in the snapshot the controller has nothing to serve

verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.group == "gateway.networking.k8s.io") | "\(.metadata.name) bundle=\(.metadata.annotations["gateway.networking.k8s.io/bundle-version"] // "-") served=\([.spec.versions[] | select(.served) | .name] | join(","))"'  # the installed Gateway API CRD bundle version and the API versions each route CRD still serves
coversNotes: v3.0.0 (CRD Updates): Action : Please apply the latest CRD definitions
